production_batch: Batch A: Desk and whiteboard, solo
working_title: "Walk us through your creative process" (the Notes app reveal)

missing_data: metrics_source_url (view count comes from the vidIQ index, not a public page)

research_analysis.exact_observed_hook: No speech. On-screen text: "“Servers are down we lost all our data”" (top) and "Me on my first day at Microsoft" (bottom).
research_analysis.visual_hook: A man stands at a computer station in a clinical scanning room, hands on keyboard and mouse, looking nervous.
research_analysis.narrative_structure: Two static text lines set a high-stakes premise for 8 seconds. He holds a nervous look, then one camera pan lands on the monitor, which shows the visual punchline. No cuts, no speech, music only.
research_analysis.viral_mechanism: The text makes a serious claim, the face sells it, and the pan to a screen replaces the claim with something small and harmless. The viewer has to read the screen to get the joke, which forces a pause or a rewatch on an 8-second clip.
research_analysis.observed_evidence: 19.5M views on an account with 2.3K followers and a 5.8K median (3378.7x). 8.54 seconds, 0 cuts, no dialogue, no CTA. Posted 2026-11-13, the day of a Microsoft outage, and the caption uses outage hashtags.
research_analysis.performance_hypothesis: Hypothesis: most of the spread came from the news day, but the structure (claim, nervous face, pan to a screen that undercuts it) is what made it sendable. Viewers rewatch to read the monitor and send it to coworkers with 'me'. Without a news peg expect a fraction of the views, so the adaptation leans on Alex's own 13.5M proof instead of a brand event.
research_analysis.why_this_format_fits_alex: Same grammar as his two biggest Reels: one shot, no speech, one line of text, under 10 seconds (Central Park 13.5M, travel hack 3.6M). The reveal can point at his own Central Park hit, so a profile visitor immediately finds the pinned video and sees what he does.
research_analysis.originality_changes: Borrowed: text premise plus nervous hold plus single pan to a screen that deflates the premise. New: the premise is a client asking about his creative process, the screen is his own Notes app, the subject is his real 13.5M Reel, and there is no news event or brand.

alex_adaptation.concept: A client asks the 23-year-old agency owner to explain the creative process behind a 13.5M-view video. The camera pans to his laptop: the entire process is one badly typed note.
alex_adaptation.target_audience: Non-followers 18-34 who make content, freelance, or work in marketing, plus anyone who saw the Central Park Reel.
alex_adaptation.primary_emotion: Amusement at a confident-looking professional being exposed
alex_adaptation.first_frame: Alex seated at his desk in a collared shirt, hands frozen above the laptop keyboard, eyes wide at the camera. Two text lines already on screen.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.action: Sits upright, professional. Eyes locked on camera, lips pressed, the face of someone asked a question on a call he cannot answer. One slow blink.
full_script.camera: Phone on tripod, chest-up, laptop edge visible at bottom right of frame.
full_script.on_screen_text: Top: Client: "Walk us through your creative process" / Bottom: Me, 13.5 million views later:
full_script.editing: No cut. Text on from frame 1.
full_script.audio: Light staccato strings or a ticking-clock style royalty-free track, starts on frame 1.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.action: Tiny nervous swallow. Eyes flick down to the laptop and back to camera as if deciding whether to show it. Very slight head shake.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.action: He reaches forward and turns the tripod himself (hand enters frame) so the camera pans from his face to the laptop screen.
full_script.camera: Single pan right and slightly down, ends on the laptop screen filling the frame. Lock focus on the screen before filming.
full_script.on_screen_text: Same two lines stay up, positioned so they do not cover the note.
full_script.editing: No cut. If the pan blurs, speed-ramp it slightly rather than cutting.

full_script.speaker: Alex
full_script.action: Screen shows the Notes app. One note titled 'ideas'. Body, in lowercase: 'central park but its a parking lot ???' and under it 'ask mom if funny'. Cursor blinking.
full_script.camera: Static on screen, text large enough to read on a phone (zoom Notes to 200%).
full_script.editing: End the clip on the screen with no button so it loops back to his face.
full_script.audio: Music cuts on the last frame.

alternate_hooks: Top: "How long did the 13.5M video take to plan?" / Bottom: Me, a professional:
Top: Brand: "Send over the strategy deck" / Bottom: The strategy deck:
Top: "You must have a whole team for this" / Bottom: The team:
alternate_endings: The note has a second line dated the same day: 'update: 13.5M. do not tell client how.'
Pan lands on the laptop, which is closed. A sticky note on the lid reads 'central park = parking lot?'. Pan back to his face, he shrugs once.
alex_adaptation.caption: Three weeks of strategy. #marketing
alex_adaptation.call_to_action: None. The pinned Central Park Reel is the payoff for anyone who taps the profile.

props: Laptop with Notes app open at 200% zoom
production.wardrobe: Collared shirt, neat hair, the 'on a client call' look
shot_list: One continuous take: 5 s on face, 2 s pan, 2 s on screen. Shoot 5 takes.
production.editor_instructions: No cuts. Add both text lines for the full duration, white with black stroke, top line in quotes. Keep the note fully unobstructed in the last 2 seconds. Trim so the last frame is the readable note. Export 9 s.

variants_to_test: Alternate hook: "You must have a whole team for this" / The team:
Alternate payoff: second note line 'update: 13.5M. do not tell client how.'
testing.promotion_decision: Brand fit 3: promote if 48h views are at least 3x the trailing median and follows per 1,000 reached or shares per 1,000 reached land in the top quartile; if follows per 1,000 are 2x median at low views, refilm with the 'team' hook.
follow_up_variations_if_successful: Same pan, screen shows a Slack-style message to himself: 'great idea Alex' 'thanks Alex'
"What tools do you use?" pan to a phone with a cracked screen and a roll of tape used as a tripod
"Who approved this concept?" pan to a group chat where the only reply is his mom's thumbs up

creative_confidence.score_type: Subjective production-priority score, not predicted viral probability
creative_confidence.rationale: Matches his proven silent one-shot format and points every viewer at his best Reel. The reference had a news tailwind this version will not have, so the upside is lower than 19.5M suggests, but the cost is 20 minutes.
uncertainties: The reference's views were tied to a same-day Microsoft outage; the mechanism is untested without a news peg.
The note text must be readable on a small phone; test before posting.
Viewers who have not seen the Central Park Reel still get the joke only if '13.5 million views' reads clearly.
